narration.text: A document has a beginning, a middle and an end. Here we can read a life, from early puzzles to the work that survived its author.
Beneath that sequence lies another structure. Dodgson, the mathematician, the author. What if we could follow the person through all those words?
A table of contents tells us how a document has been organised. Follow Photography and we arrive at the section the author gave that name.
A semantic inventory gathers the things that appear across those sections. Five expressions for the same person give us a single entry, Lewis Carroll.

caption: Survey the document in its wider context.

narration.text: How often do we meet Carroll? Five times in this document. Each annotation counts as one mention here, even when the wording changes.
Beside that live count is a different measure. Across the knowledge base, the database counts saved, indexed annotation segments. Unsaved changes stay local.
Look at photography. Three of its four recorded references are here. Mathematics appears just once here, yet turns up throughout the collection.
Knowing that a person occurs five times is one thing. Seeing where is another. Hover over Lewis Carroll and watch the words in the document.
Dodgson. The mathematician. The author. Carroll. Lewis Carroll. Different expressions light up together because each already points to the same person.
Move away and the light recedes. Try photography, then Oxford. The light moves while the words stay where they were.

caption: Step back to see the distribution.

narration.text: From a little farther away, the individual words give way to a pattern. Carroll runs through the sketch.
Photography gathers near the middle and returns at the end. Oxford connects two distant passages. We can see their spacing at a glance.

caption: Focus brings the marked passages together.

narration.text: Sometimes we want to do more than locate a reference. What does this sketch actually say about photography?
Follow the marked passages. The camera enters during the Oxford years. Later we meet the demands of the practice and, at the end, its legacy.
Now focus on photography. Watch the space between the marked passages contract. The three passages keep their size and their order.
Read them together. The document concertinas around the subject of our attention.

caption: Release the focus to recover the full sketch.

narration.text: Release the focus. Each passage returns to its place in the sketch. Now choose Oxford. Teaching and remembrance come together.
Open the document again and follow Alice Liddell. A sitter in one passage becomes the listener to a story in another.
The author wrote one sequence. As readers, we can follow several threads through it.

caption: The same links support three ways of reading.

narration.text: Recall the connections made while writing. The author and Dodgson were both linked to Lewis Carroll.
Those links let us survey the people in the sketch, illuminate their words, and concentrate on the passages that mention them. Our earlier acts of annotation become instruments of reading.
Release the focus once more. The document responds to the interests of its reader while preserving the composition of its author.
One document. Many readings.
